title: Token-bucket desync causes spurious throttles and incorrect accounting
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Several customers reported sudden spikes in throttling and unexpected token consumption that did not match traced request volume. Investigation shows mismatch between in-memory bucket accumulators (per-route and per-org) and persisted metering counters leading to: 1) transient spurious throttles for bursts that should have fit policy, and 2) duplicate accounting of a small percentage of requests during route fallback and autoscale events. This ticket tracks the diagnostics, mitigation, and a code fix to ensure deterministic enforcement and one-to-one accounting between enforcement path and billing events.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure per-org global quota with a permissive per-route override (higher per-route burst).
2) Simulate a mix of short-chat and long-generation requests with synthetic client using 50 concurrent connections ramping to burst for 60s.
3) Trigger route failover by briefly disabling primary worker pool to cause request reroute to compatible model variant.
4) Observe: certain requests get 429s despite headroom in aggregated counters; billing dashboard shows ~0.8% more tokens accounted than produced during the window.
root_cause_summary: Race between async in-memory token-bucket delta flush and fallback request path. We maintain independent per-route and per-org accumulators and flush deltas to the persistent metering store on a cadence (100ms). When a request is retried or rerouted during a flush window, both the route-level and org-level delta flush can include the same request's token usage (race on nominally idempotent delta). Additionally, a stale policy-cache TTL (30s) caused enforcement to check an older quota object and temporarily apply stricter burst windows that rejected otherwise-allowed requests. Clock skew between nodes exacerbated the window alignment leading to double-counting in a measurable subset of events.
proposed_fix: 1) Introduce per-request token attribution id (UUID) used by both route and org flush paths to deduplicate deltas in the metering store; 2) make delta flushes idempotent by writing per-attribution records and aggregating during finalization instead of naive add; 3) reduce policy-cache TTL to 5s and add short-circuit revalidation on route fallback; 4) add integration test harness (load-test + failover) and QA long-run job to validate accounting drift under synthetic workloads.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Miguel Torres: Initial triage. Reproduced locally with load harness. Spikes correlated to route failover timeline and flush cadence. Temporary mitigation: increased flush interval to 200ms to reduce dual-flush window (not acceptable as long-term change).

2026-02-18 - Sophie Nguyen: Added detailed trace capture around token accounting paths. Found shared codepath that doesn't mark per-request attribution when fallback path is executed. Created PR #3456 to add attribution id to the request lifecycle.

2026-02-20 - Priya Shah (PM): Notified three customers impacted; provided temporary guidance to disable route-level tight burst rules until fix lands. Customers requested export of affected request ids for audit — engineering to provide via console export.

2026-02-22 - Sophie Nguyen: Integration tests show accounting drift reduced from ~0.8% to <0.01% with PR #3456 changes. Edge case remains when metering store experiences transient 5xx and client retries are auto-replayed by LB. Added retry dedupe by attribution id in PR #3489.

2026-02-26 - Security review: confirmed no PII in attribution ids; audit log will reference attribution ids and original request id mapping. Security owner @Liu Wei requested a short design note — linked in Confluence.

2026-02-28 - Miguel Torres: Deployed staged rollout of changes to canary region. Observability panels show errors down 95% and token-overcount eliminated in canary. Preparing rollout plan for staged ramp to prod in next 72 hours.
2026-03-01 - Sophie Nguyen: Follow-up: created long-run job (12-hour soak) for canary. If green for 48h, schedule merge to main and release in runtime-1.20.
notes: Follow-up items: backfill missing attribution for historical windows (analytics-only fix) + accounting reconciliation job. Timeline: analytics job to run after release and produce CSV for billing reconciliation.

Edge cases: cross-region routed requests where attribution id was not propagated across the proxy chain. Plan: propagate attribution header and add a validating middleware to drop non-propagated cases for counting rather than double-counting.
Related tickets: ENG-19876 (stale-policy-cache-per-org-rollout) — we pulled the TTL change into this ticket to avoid split ownership during urgent fix window.
